issues.detail: Hebrew 'אֲתֹנֹות צְחֹרֹות' means 'white donkeys' (female donkeys that are white/tawny), but Chinese renders as '驢子' (donkeys) without the color 'white' (白色). This omits the substantive descriptor 'צְחֹרֹות'.

Hebrew 'יֹשְׁבֵי עַל מִדִּין' means 'those who sit on a saddle/rug' (מִדִּין = saddle-cloth or carpet), but Chinese renders as '坐在審判座上' (sitting on a judgment seat), which adds the concept of 'judgment' (審判) not present in the Hebrew and changes the meaning.
